counterexample: In the proof's own one-dimensional model, suppose the observed first incident is at t=0.55. Sending closest ambulance C gives expected two-incident travel (1-0.55)+E[t_2]=0.45+0.50=0.95, because only the two left ambulances remain. Sending A gives 0.55+E[min(t_2,1-t_2)]=0.55+0.25=0.80. More generally, when 1/2<t<5/8, sending A is better despite C being closer. Thus a policy that sends A only on that interval beats always dispatching the closest ambulance.
